title: Perfect matchings in regular bipartite graphs
statement: Let $G$ be a simple graph on a finite vertex set that is bipartite with parts $X$ and $Y$, so that every edge of $G$ joins a vertex of $X$ to a vertex of $Y$. If there is an integer $k > 0$ such that every vertex of $G$ has degree exactly $k$, then $G$ admits a perfect matching: a set of edges that is vertex-disjoint and covers every vertex of $G$.
hypotheses_covered: G is bipartite with parts X and Y
k-regular (every vertex has degree exactly k)
conclusion: existence of a perfect matching
